name: short-form-captions guidelines
about: Caption timing and length limits from published subtitle guidelines, each with the guideline's own words and the day it was read. A rule's level is fail when the source states it as a limit or a requirement, warn when the source recommends or gives it as a guide. These are the publishers' rules for their own programmes, used as a sourced yardstick for short video; no app requires them.

netflix-general.title: Timed Text Style Guide: General Requirements

netflix-timing.title: Timed Text Style Guide: Subtitle Timing Guidelines

netflix.name: Netflix, English (USA) SDH (same-language captions), adult programs

rules.quote: Adult programs: Up to 20 characters per second
Minimum duration: 5/6 (five-sixths) of a second per subtitle event (e.g. 20 frames for 24fps)
Maximum duration: 7 seconds per subtitle event
Subtitles must have a minimum of 2 frames between them. This parameter is applicable to any frame rate of content.
In 24fps content, any gaps between subtitles of 3-11 frames inclusive must be closed to 2 frames.
Gaps between subtitles should either be 2 frames or half a second or more.

netflix-children.name: Netflix, English (USA) SDH (same-language captions), children's programs

rules.quote: Children’s programs: Up to 17 characters per second

bbc.name: BBC, landscape or square video (37 characters is the broadcast Teletext limit; online the limit is a width)

rules.quote: broadcast 37 characters, reduced if coloured text is used
rules.note: Teletext's limit, used here as a guide: online the BBC limits a line by width (68% of a 16:9 frame), not by characters.

rules.quote: For landscape or square (16:9, 4:3 or 1:1) video, a maximum subtitle length of two lines is recommended.
The recommended subtitle speed is 160-180 words-per-minute (WPM) or 0.33 to 0.375 second per word.
you should aim to leave a subtitle on screen for a minimum period of around 0.3 seconds per word (e.g. 1.2 seconds for a 4-word subtitle)
As a guide, the equivalent to 37 characters in a 75% width region of a 16:9 (landscape) video is 25 characters in a 90% width region of a 9:16 (vertical) video.
For vertical (9:16) video, a maximum subtitle length of three lines is recommended.
